description: A place east of the Jordan where Jacob, returning to Canaan, was met by angels and named the site "two camps" (Genesis 32:1-2). It later became Ish-bosheth's capital when Abner made him king over Israel against David (2 Samuel 2:8-9), and still later the refuge David fled to during Absalom's rebellion, where he received support from Machir and Barzillai (2 Samuel 17:24-27).
family_friendly_summary: Mahanaim was a town east of the Jordan. Jacob met a company of God's angels there and named the place "two camps." Much later, King David fled to Mahanaim during his son Absalom's rebellion, and kind people like Barzillai brought him food and supplies.
